question: Why might a hospital find it hard to use primary nursing instead of team nursing?

options.A: Team nursing requires every single staff member to hold a master's degree.
options.B: Primary nursing completely eliminates the need for any communication with doctors.
options.C: Team nursing prevents nurses from ever talking to patients or families.
options.D: Primary nursing requires a larger proportion of registered nurses, which increases staffing costs.

explanation: Primary nursing needs lots of qualified Registered Nurses to give that individualized care, which can be expensive for hospital management compared to mixing in more junior staff. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T3#GNS123_U1_T3_h4)

question: How should you apply skin antiseptic before putting in an IV line?

options.A: Scrub back and forth rapidly over the exact insertion point only.
options.B: Apply the antiseptic and immediately wipe it dry with sterile gauze.
options.C: Start at the center of the site and wipe outward in concentric circles.
options.D: Pour the liquid directly into the vein before inserting the needle.

explanation: Brilliant! Moving from the clean center outwards pushes germs away from the spot where the needle will enter. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h5)

question: Where is the majority of the fluid in your body actually stored?

options.A: Inside the body cells
options.B: Within the lymphatic channels
options.C: Inside the blood vessels
options.D: Surrounding the tissue cells

explanation: Great job! Most of our body water is kept safely tucked away right inside our cells (intracellular fluid). Think of it as the main water reservoir of the body! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T10#GNS121_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why are IPC rules still enforced in a quarantine zone where people feel healthy?

options.A: To test the durability of hospital cleaning supplies
options.B: Because residents might already be shedding germs before showing symptoms
options.C: To punish people for breaking travel rules
options.D: To replace the need for medical check-ups

explanation: Many infectious diseases can be transmitted by people who appear well but are in the late stages of incubation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a focus area during a health inspection survey in an SNF?

options.A: Infection control practices and hand hygiene compliance
options.B: Medication administration safety and storage
options.C: Stock market investments of the facility parent corporation
options.D: Resident rights and protection from abuse or neglect

explanation: Health inspectors look at patient safety, care quality, and resident rights—not corporate financial portfolios! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h8)

question: What does empathetic dialogue require from a nurse?

options.A: Stepping into the emotional reality of the patient
options.B: Maintaining strict professional detachment at all times
options.C: Directing the conversation toward physical symptoms only
options.D: Giving immediate advice to fix the patient's problems

explanation: Empathy requires the nurse to attempt to understand and feel with the patient rather than staying completely detached. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which part of your hand should you use to massage a patient's scalp during a shampoo?

options.A: Knuckles
options.B: Palms of the hands
options.C: Tips of the fingernails
options.D: Pads of the fingers

explanation: Always use the pads of your fingers! It cleans effectively while keeping your fingernails from scratching the patient's sensitive scalp. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which type of nerve receptor is mainly responsible for detecting tissue damage or pain?

options.A: Nociceptor
options.B: Mechanoreceptor
options.C: Chemoreceptor
options.D: Thermoreceptor

explanation: Spot on! Nociceptors are your body's early warning alarm system. They fire up when tissues experience actual or potential damage, creating the feeling of pain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h3)

question: How many total degrees are in a full circle used for a pie chart?

options.A: 360 degrees
options.B: 100 degrees
options.C: 180 degrees
options.D: 90 degrees

explanation: Spot on! A full circle is always 360 degrees all the way round. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T8#GNS217_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is a major downside of relying only on a written handover book without talking?

options.A: It is too expensive for a standard hospital ward to maintain
options.B: It lacks the interactive opportunity to ask questions or clarify details
options.C: It instantly deletes all nursing notes after eight hours
options.D: It forces patients to listen to private staff conversations

explanation: Writing is great, but nothing beats live chat where you can ask questions immediately if something about a patient's condition is confusing. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is a major economic barrier that limits a woman's healthcare autonomy?

options.A: Financial dependency on male heads of households
options.B: Too much freedom in spending personal income
options.C: An overabundance of free public health clinics
options.D: Excessive participation in local market associations

explanation: Without personal income or financial control, women often cannot afford transport fare or medical bills without male approval. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h2)

question: Why must nurses always teach postpartum women to clean their perineal area from front to back?

options.A: To stimulate faster contraction of the abdominal wall muscles
options.B: To ensure that lochia stops flowing within the first twenty-four hours
options.C: To prevent spreading bacteria from the anal region into the vagina or wound
options.D: To prevent painful swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: Wiping front to back keeps unwanted germs from the back passage away from healing tears or surgical stitches, preventing nasty infections! Simple hygiene makes a massive difference. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: A manager watches a nurse perform a sterile dressing change to ensure correct technique. What type of control is this?

options.A: Feedforward control
options.B: Concurrent control
options.C: Financial control
options.D: Feedback control

explanation: Observing care as it happens lets the manager catch and fix mistakes on the spot. That's concurrent control! [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h3)

question: Which of these details is NOT necessary to record when documenting a syringe driver setup?

options.A: The batch number of the administered drug
options.B: The patient's favorite television program
options.C: The exact location of the insertion site
options.D: The specific infusion rate set on the pump

explanation: Too easy! While knowing their favorite show is nice for conversation, it has no place in official medication documentation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h7)

question: What drives the passive movement of water across the lining of the intestines?

options.A: Osmotic gradients created by electrolyte transport
options.B: Direct pumping of water molecules by ATP pumps
options.C: Muscular churning of the large intestine
options.D: Enzymatic breakdown of dietary fiber

explanation: You're right! Water doesn't have its own active pumps in the gut; it simply follows the salt (like sodium) via osmosis—where salt goes, water flows! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T012#GNS227_U1_T012_h6)

question: Why do doctors need specific serological tests in addition to routine liver enzyme tests?

options.A: Routine enzymes cannot detect jaundice, whereas serological tests measure skin pigment
options.B: Liver enzymes show that injury is happening, but serological tests identify the exact viral cause
options.C: Serological tests are the only way to measure how much urine the patient is producing daily
options.D: Blood enzymes only work for Hepatitis A, requiring serological tests for all other diseases

explanation: Spot on! Routine liver tests tell us the liver is angry and inflamed, but serological blood tests act like detectives to tell us *which* specific virus started the fire. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h5)

question: Why is it better to help an older patient sit in a chair for meals instead of keeping them flat in bed?

options.A: It saves the nursing staff time during meal distribution
options.B: It is a strict hospital rule with no clinical reasoning behind it
options.C: It completely cures chronic joint arthritis in the legs
options.D: It prevents muscle deconditioning and improves digestion and alertness

explanation: Well done! Sitting upright helps them swallow safely, digests food better, and keeps them awake and alert. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h3)

question: How is a triage check different from a full ward admission assessment?

options.A: Triage assessment is rapid and focused on immediate life threats rather than being comprehensive
options.B: Admission assessments take less than two minutes to complete
options.C: Admission assessments are always performed by security guards instead of nurses
options.D: Triage assessment skips vital signs entirely and relies on guesswork

explanation: At triage, we don't have time for a lengthy life story. We scan for immediate dangers first, then dive deeper later! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care once a patient enters the active dying phase?

options.A: Checking blood pressure and pulse every fifteen minutes
options.B: Trying to restart vital signs with emergency medications
options.C: Ensuring absolute comfort and supporting the family
options.D: Forcing fluids by mouth to stop dehydration

explanation: When active dying begins, our focus shifts completely from trying to cure to keeping the patient comfortable and wrapping the family in support. You are doing amazing! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h6)

question: What does the maternal mortality ratio actually measure?

options.A: Total deaths of women of childbearing age
options.B: Infant deaths per 1,000 live births
options.C: Deaths per 1,000 pregnant women
options.D: Deaths per 100,000 live births

explanation: Think of it this way: the maternal mortality ratio tells us how many mothers we lose for every 100,000 live births. Super important metric in public health! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h2)

question: Why should community nutrition counseling respect local food traditions?

options.A: Families are much more likely to follow advice that fits their culture
options.B: Traditional recipes always contain zero nutritional value
options.C: Cultural habits prevent any form of weight gain
options.D: Nurses are legally forbidden from discussing local foods

explanation: When you work with a family's cultural food habits instead of fighting them, they are way more likely to stick with your healthy changes! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T19#GNS214_U1_T19_h7)

question: A patient comes to your clinic with severe watery diarrhea and sudden, rapid dehydration after eating food from a roadside vendor. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Asthma exacerbation
options.C: Chronic hypertension
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: You nailed it. Sudden, severe watery diarrhea and rapid dehydration after eating questionable food are classic red flags for cholera. Quick fluid replacement is key here! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h3)

question: Which of the following is a well-formulated SMART objective for a community health project?

options.A: To improve the general lifestyle and happiness of all market women
options.B: To train 40 traditional birth attendants in safe delivery practices within three months
options.C: To make sure nobody in the entire state ever gets sick with cholera again
options.D: To talk to people about sanitation whenever nurses have free time

explanation: This statement is specific, has a clear number, and includes a strict timeframe, making it truly SMART. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: What makes a Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) so great for a busy rural health clinic?

options.A: It gives quick results from a finger-prick blood sample without complex equipment
options.B: It permanently prevents future mosquito bites from causing infection
options.C: It is the only test capable of identifying dead parasites after treatment
options.D: It tells the nurse the exact number of parasites circulating in the blood

explanation: Spot on! RDTs are fast, portable, and a lifesaver in clinics where there are no fancy lab machines or steady electricity. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which dimension of holistic care involves a person's sense of meaning, purpose, and faith?

options.A: Spiritual dimension
options.B: Physical dimension
options.C: Social dimension
options.D: Mental dimension

explanation: The spiritual dimension connects a patient to their core values, life purpose, and faith traditions. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the correct order for putting on (donning) your PPE before entering an isolation room?

options.A: Mask first, then gloves, gown, and eye protection
options.B: Gloves first, then gown, mask, and protective eyewear
options.C: Eye protection first, followed by gloves, gown, and mask
options.D: Gown first, then mask or respirator, eye protection, and gloves

explanation: Great job! You start by covering your body with the gown, secure your breathing and eyes, and pull your glove cuffs over the gown sleeves last so there are no skin gaps. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which level of prevention involves giving childhood immunizations to stop disease before it starts?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention aims to prevent disease or injury before it ever occurs through measures like immunizations and health education. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is staff wellness included as a key part of school health programs?

options.A: Teachers serve as role models whose health habits influence students
options.B: Teachers are legally required to pass annual fitness tests
options.C: School staff require more medical leave than regular workers
options.D: Staff members pay for the maintenance of school clinics

explanation: You nailed it! Children copy the adults around them, so healthy teachers naturally encourage good habits in their pupils. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h2)

question: An infant receives a vaccine four weeks too early. What is the correct nursing action?

options.A: Perform a blood test immediately to measure antibody levels
options.B: Administer a double dose at the next clinic visit to balance the schedule
options.C: Repeat the dose after the correct minimum interval has passed
options.D: Assume the child is fully protected and skip all future boosters

explanation: Doses given too early often don't count because the baby's system isn't quite ready or maternal antibodies block them. We simply repeat it at the right time to keep them safe. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T70#GNS214_U1_T70_h5)

question: Which health areas in Nigeria have traditionally received the most support from international donor agencies?

options.A: Geriatric care facilities for retired politicians
options.B: Private cosmetic surgery and dental implant clinics
options.C: Orthopedic workshops for sports injuries
options.D: Infectious diseases, immunization, and maternal health programs

explanation: Global partners like WHO or USAID heavily target public health priorities like HIV/AIDS, malaria, and vaccines. Keep this public health focus in mind! [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is your main job as a clinic nurse when it comes to family planning reporting?

options.A: Purchasing international medical supplies directly
options.B: Manufacturing contraceptive commodities for the district
options.C: Auditing national health ministry budgets annually
options.D: Gathering and recording service data at the clinic level

explanation: You've got this! Nurses right there at the clinic are the vital first link in capturing client visits and service data accurately. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h1)

question: What is the main difference between an acute kidney injury and chronic renal failure?

options.A: Chronic renal failure always resolves completely with proper hydration therapy.
options.B: Acute injury develops slowly over several years without causing any symptoms.
options.C: Acute injury only affects the bladder, while chronic failure affects the entire ureter.
options.D: Chronic renal failure involves permanent and irreversible loss of nephron function.

explanation: You've got this! Chronic renal failure causes permanent scarring and loss of nephrons over time. Acute injury, on the other hand, can often be reversed if caught early. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why should a nurse always recommend locally available and affordable foods when giving diet advice?

options.A: It ensures the client can maintain the diet long-term
options.B: It guarantees that the food contains zero calories
options.C: It replaces the need for any professional medical care
options.D: It prevents the client from ever needing clean water

explanation: You got it! Good advice has to be practical. If people can't find or afford the food nearby, they won't be able to keep up with the diet. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T011#GNS227_U2_T011_h7)

question: A patient with a recent stroke begins leaking stool unconsciously. What is the most likely underlying cause?

options.A: Primary infection of the internal anal lining
options.B: Neurological damage disrupting normal bowel signaling
options.C: Complete loss of rectal tissue elasticity
options.D: Severe physical injury to the external sphincter muscle

explanation: Strokes affect the central nervous system pathways that control voluntary bowel function, leading to reflex emptying without conscious control. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which problem-solving model focuses on looking backward after an error to find underlying system failures?

options.A: Random brainstorming
options.B: Trial and error
options.C: Immediate punishment
options.D: Root cause analysis

explanation: Root cause analysis investigates why an incident happened by looking at underlying workplace or system processes. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why are regular developmental check-ups by a nurse so important during a baby's first year?

options.A: It replaces the need for any laboratory blood tests or physical examinations
options.B: It proves whether the parents caused the infant's developmental injuries
options.C: It accurately predicts the exact adult height the child will eventually reach
options.D: It helps catch early signs of neurological delays so interventions can start promptly

explanation: Catching delays early lets therapy start when a baby's brain is still developing rapidly and can adapt best! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing an ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: To check the outer muscles that move the eyeball around
options.B: To view the internal structures of the back of the eye
options.C: To test the patient for clear distance and reading vision
options.D: To measure the exact fluid pressure inside the eyeball

explanation: Ophthalmoscopy specifically directs light through the pupil to examine the internal fundus, which includes the retina and optic disc. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why should standard cloth or fabric tailors' tapes be avoided in clinical practice?

options.A: They only measure in inches rather than centimeters
options.B: They are too expensive for community clinics
options.C: They stretch over time and give false readings
options.D: They dissolve easily when exposed to skin moisture

explanation: Fabric stretches with repeated pulling, which ruins the accuracy required for precise health tracking. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h2)

question: What is the best way to learn about a family's cultural or religious death traditions?

options.A: Ignore cultural practices to maintain strict hospital routines
options.B: Ask open-ended questions to learn about their specific preferences
options.C: Insist that hospital customs always override personal traditions
options.D: Assume all families from the same country share identical beliefs

explanation: Never assume! Always ask open, respectful questions so you can learn what matters most to that specific family. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T8#GNS221_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is the maximum expected duration for normal postpartum blues before they should resolve?

options.A: Forty-eight hours
options.B: One year
options.C: Six months
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: Postpartum blues typically peak around the fourth or fifth day and resolve spontaneously within the first two weeks after delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h6)

question: A patient requesting a medical abortion is found to have an IUD in place. What needs to happen first?

options.A: The patient must be switched immediately to a surgical procedure.
options.B: The medications can be given safely around the IUD.
options.C: The IUD must be removed before starting the medications.
options.D: Progesterone supplements should be given to offset the IUD.

explanation: Well done! Any existing intrauterine device (IUD) needs to be removed before starting the regimen to lower the risk of severe infection and make sure the medication works properly. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h2)

question: How is Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) viewed under international human rights law?

options.A: An acceptable alternative traditional medicine practice
options.B: A mandatory cultural initiation rite for minors
options.C: A violation of human rights and bodily integrity
options.D: A minor surgical procedure with health benefits

explanation: Spot on! Global human rights laws recognize FGM as an act of violence that strips women and children of their fundamental right to physical safety and health. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T5#GNS225_U6_T5_h1)

question: Where is the classic pain of acute pancreatitis felt, and where does it usually spread?

options.A: Chest region radiating to the left arm
options.B: Upper abdomen radiating to the back
options.C: Suprapubic area radiating to the lower back
options.D: Lower right abdomen radiating to the thigh

explanation: Spot on! Pancreatic pain is notorious for being felt right in the upper belly and boring straight through to the back. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h3)

question: During a home visit, a nurse notices a child with autism is locked indoors because the family feels ashamed. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Report the parents to the police for immediate imprisonment without talking to them
options.B: Provide education, reduce stigma, and connect the family with support groups
options.C: Transfer the child to an adult surgical ward
options.D: Ignore the situation as a private family matter

explanation: As nurses, we lead with empathy! We educate families to lift the burden of stigma and gently connect them to helpful support networks. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T7#GNS225_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is the main reason a nurse uses the Braden Scale when a resident is admitted?

options.A: Measuring the severity of cognitive memory loss
options.B: Determining the level of financial independence
options.C: Evaluating the daily nutritional caloric intake
options.D: Assessing the risk of developing pressure injuries

explanation: Awesome! The Braden Scale is a fantastic, standard nursing tool used to predict and prevent skin breakdown. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T12#GNS324_U5_T12_h4)

question: How do hookworm larvae usually enter the human body?

options.A: Bites from infected mosquitoes
options.B: Drinking unboiled river water
options.C: Direct penetration through the skin
options.D: Inhalation of airborne dust particles

explanation: Hookworm larvae love hanging out in contaminated soil. When people walk barefoot, these tiny worms can actually burrow right through the skin. Good reason to wear sandals! [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a negative consequence of child marriage for a young girl?

options.A: Severe psychological trauma and social isolation
options.B: Permanent immunity against sexually transmitted infections
options.C: High risk of early adolescent pregnancy complications
options.D: Abrupt termination of her formal education

explanation: Correct! Child marriage definitely does not grant immunity to infections; starting sexual activity early often raises that risk instead. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of preparing a patient for community reintegration before hospital discharge?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the hospital nursing staff
options.B: To test if the patient can survive without any medical supplies
options.C: To fulfill mandatory paperwork requirements for health insurance
options.D: To ensure a smooth and safe transition back to home and daily routines

explanation: Community reintegration focuses on equipping the patient and home environment for real-world independence and participation. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to healthcare access in Nigerian communities?

options.A: Gender inequality limiting women's health choices
options.B: Poverty and inability to pay for medications
options.C: An oversupply of free universal healthcare facilities in every village
options.D: Stigma and discrimination against stigmatized health conditions

explanation: Spot on! Having too many free clinics is definitely not our problem—scarcity, poverty, and cost are the real barriers. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T15#GNS312_U4_T15_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you should do when someone asks you a drug-related question?

options.A: Consulting a tertiary drug reference textbook
options.B: Formulating the final verbal response for the doctor
options.C: Searching the primary medical literature for clinical trials
options.D: Securing demographic and background data about the patient and requester

explanation: Spot on! Before you can hunt for an answer, you need to know who is asking and the patient's specific health situation. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T3#GNS215_U2_T3_h3)

question: Leaving a surgical swab inside a patient is legally considered what kind of error?

options.A: An unavoidable accident
options.B: Minor administrative error
options.C: Professional negligence
options.D: Standard therapeutic risk

explanation: It's a preventable mistake, which is why proper counting protocols are taken so seriously in nursing practice and law. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h6)

question: Which schedule describes substances with NO accepted medical use and high abuse risk?

options.A: Schedule V
options.B: Schedule IV
options.C: Schedule I
options.D: Schedule II

explanation: Schedule I drugs are considered too dangerous and lack approved medical applications. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why does a nurse monitor the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) for a patient receiving heparin?

options.A: To measure the exact number of active platelets in the bloodstream
options.B: To check if the patient has developed an iron deficiency anemia
options.C: To ensure the intrinsic and common pathways are appropriately suppressed
options.D: To evaluate how well the liver is producing new red blood cells

explanation: Heparin affects the intrinsic pathway, so checking the aPTT lets the nurse know if the drug dose is safe and effective. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why must nurses strictly avoid giving aspirin or ibuprofen to a yellow fever patient?

options.A: They cause the body temperature to spike dangerously high
options.B: They increase the risk of severe bleeding and hemorrhage
options.C: They destroy remaining healthy cells in the liver and kidneys
options.D: They neutralize the effectiveness of prescribed intravenous fluids

explanation: That's right! Yellow fever messes with normal blood clotting, and drugs like ibuprofen make bleeding way worse. Always check before giving pain meds! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h6)

question: How do barrier methods like condoms actually prevent STIs?

options.A: To permanently neutralize circulating viral loads in the bloodstream
options.B: To increase local mucosal immunity against parasitic invasion
options.C: To block the exchange of infectious bodily fluids during intercourse
options.D: To destroy bacterial cell walls upon contact in the vaginal canal

explanation: You got it! Condoms act as a physical shield so infectious fluids don't pass between partners. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why do doctors often combine NK1 blockers and steroids with 5-HT3 drugs for patients on strong chemotherapy?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for intravenous fluid replacement
options.B: They prevent hair loss caused by aggressive cytotoxic medications
options.C: They neutralize the chemotherapy drugs before they damage the stomach
options.D: They target multiple distinct pathways to prevent both acute and delayed nausea

explanation: You nailed it! Hitting different receptors at the same time gives the best defense against tough, multi-day chemotherapy nausea. Teamwork in pharmacology! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T6#GNS223_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why do nurses encourage new mothers to walk around soon after delivery (early ambulation)?

options.A: To completely eliminate white blood cells from circulation
options.B: To stimulate the kidneys to stop producing erythropoietin
options.C: To help prevent dangerous blood clots in the deep veins
options.D: To immediately restore the pre-pregnancy plasma volume

explanation: Get those legs moving! Walking helps blood circulate properly and stops clots from forming in the legs after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h7)

question: What can happen if a nursing research study uses a sample size that is far too small?

options.A: The statistical software will refuse to run any calculations
options.B: Every patient in the hospital will be forced to participate
options.C: The researcher might miss a real and important clinical effect
options.D: The study will automatically cost too much money to complete

explanation: Spot on! If your group of patients is too tiny, your study won't have enough power to spot a real pattern or treatment benefit. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h5)

question: A resident is scheduled for discharge next month. What should the care team arrange before departure?

options.A: Termination of all follow-up medical care
options.B: Immediate readmission to an acute psychiatric ward
options.C: Outpatient therapy appointments and secure housing
options.D: A police record check for employment eligibility

explanation: Wonderful! Good discharge planning means setting up safe housing and ongoing outpatient support beforehand to ensure a smooth transition and prevent relapse. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h8)

question: What is a major physical danger resulting from unsafe abortion procedures in teenagers?

options.A: Uterine perforation and severe hemorrhage
options.B: Immediate resolution of pelvic pain
options.C: Enhanced cardiovascular output
options.D: Permanent increase in bone density

options.C: Order an emergency surgical dilation and curettage procedure

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Reassuring her that amenorrhea is a harmless side effect eases her mind and keeps her from dropping a great contraceptive method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h6)

question: During which of the following periods can mother-to-child transmission of HIV NOT occur?

options.A: Postnatally while the infant is breastfeeding
options.B: Pre-conception before fertilization takes place
options.C: Intrapartum during the actual labor and delivery
options.D: In utero during the course of the pregnancy

explanation: Transmission requires active exposure during pregnancy, delivery, or through breast milk; it does not happen before conception occurs. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h2)

question: Why is it important to document whether the patient's pupils were dilated during the ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: It measures the exact neurological response speed of the brain
options.B: It explains how well the internal structures could be visualized
options.C: It prevents the next nurse from checking the visual acuity score
options.D: It proves that the correct eye drop dosage was billed to insurance

explanation: Pupillary dilation changes how much of the fundus is visible, so documenting dilation provides essential context for the examination findings. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h9)

question: What is a very common cause of accidental needle-stick injuries during a busy shift?

options.A: Transporting sealed waste boxes
options.B: Attempting to recap used needles
options.C: Washing non-sterile kidney dishes
options.D: Checking intravenous infusion lines

explanation: Trying to put the cap back on a used needle with two hands is a recipe for a missed cap and a finger prick. Never recap! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for a mother who chooses not to breastfeed?

options.A: Applying warm compresses continuously to speed up Lactogenesis II
options.B: Encouraging frequent manual expression to prevent ductal calcification
options.C: Administering large doses of synthetic oxytocin to trigger involution
options.D: Suppressive care to minimize discomfort and discourage milk production

explanation: If a mother isn't nursing, our goal is to keep her comfortable while helping her body dry up the milk supply safely—using things like firm supportive bras and avoiding breast stimulation. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h8)

question: Why is it so important to interview a patient alone when checking for gender-based violence?

options.A: To comply with laboratory protocols for collecting blood samples
options.B: To prevent the abuser from intimidating the patient or blocking disclosure
options.C: To allow the doctor to perform a physical examination faster
options.D: To speed up the hospital admission and bed allocation process

explanation: Spot on! Abusers often tag along to control the narrative. Speaking alone gives the patient a safe space to talk freely. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is the main feature of a fixed cost in a hospital?

options.A: It changes directly with the number of admissions
options.B: It is always paid using foreign currency
options.C: It remains the same regardless of patient volume
options.D: It only applies to surgical ward supplies

explanation: Fixed costs stay steady month after month, whether your ward is completely empty or packed to the brim with admissions. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h4)

question: In the SMART criteria for writing good objectives, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Measurable
options.B: Methodological
options.C: Medical
options.D: Mandatory

explanation: The 'M' stands for Measurable. It ensures your objective includes clear indicators you can actually count, observe, or evaluate! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h5)

question: What is an important nursing check before preparing an infant for a scheduled circumcision?

options.A: Starting an intravenous line in the foot
options.B: Checking when the baby last fed
options.C: Shaving the entire pubic and scrotal hair
options.D: Administering a full dose of oral antibiotics

explanation: Checking the last feeding time helps prevent the baby from vomiting and potentially choking (aspirating) while being handled during the procedure. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h4)

question: A mother is worried because her baby had a mild fever and swelling after their last shot. How should you respond?

options.A: Advise the mother never to bring the child back for any future immunizations
options.B: Report the child to public health authorities for failing a routine check
options.C: Explain that these mild reactions are normal signs of the immune system working
options.D: Immediately prescribe strong oral antibiotics to treat an expected infection

explanation: Spot on! A little soreness or low-grade fever just means the baby's immune system is busy building up its defenses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h8)

question: Why is it important to encourage a laboring mother to empty her bladder often?

options.A: Urine samples must be tested every hour during home births
options.B: It stops the uterus from contracting too strongly
options.C: It prevents the development of chronic urinary tract infections
options.D: A full bladder can obstruct fetal descent and slow down labor

explanation: Think of the bladder like a roadblock in the pelvis! Emptying it clears the way so the baby's head can move down smoothly. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the main type of tissue you will find in the hypodermis?

options.A: Adipose tissue
options.B: Skeletal muscle
options.C: Dense regular tissue
options.D: Stratified epithelium

explanation: Correct! The hypodermis is packed with adipose (fat) tissue, which helps keep us warm, stores energy, and cushions us from bumps. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h4)
